title: RuneScape animation project aims to bring Gielinor to the screen
summary:
The fantasy world of RuneScape could gain a new audience through animation. Lyrical Animation is developing a series based on the game in partnership with its developer, Jagex, and online creator Charlie White, known as MoistCr1TiKaL.

Jagex chief executive Jon Bellamy announced the project on Saturday on stage at RuneFest in Birmingham, UK. It would bring Gielinor, the setting for RuneScape's adventures, to the screen. Bellamy described it as part of a wider ambition to expand the fictional world beyond games.

Jagex first released RuneScape in 2001. It is a multiplayer online role-playing game: many people play over the internet, taking on characters within a shared world. Players explore, complete quests, take part in combat and cooperate on adventures in a medieval fantasy setting.

The franchise, a group of related titles, now includes RuneScape, Old School RuneScape and RuneScape Dragonwilds. Bellamy said players had helped shape its characters and stories over 25 years. He hopes new projects can appeal both to people who already know Gielinor and to newcomers.

White is a longtime member of the game's community. He said he had played for 22 years and was excited to work on a favorite fictional property. Across his channels and platforms, he has more than 25 million followers.

Lyrical Animation will produce the project with White's Meatier Productions. Its creative director, Daniel Dominguez, highlighted RuneScape's combination of humor and insight as a quality he wanted to bring to life.

Work remains at an early stage, and the company expects to reveal more details in 2027.
why_it_matters: The project shows how a game's fictional world can be adapted for another medium. Bellamy hopes it will reach both existing players and newcomers.
